hero.description: Aditya Shah is a Hosting Support Manager and DevOps Engineer at WPMU DEV, a community manager who has organized WordPress Bhopal since 2015, and a WordCamp speaker on WordPress security, WP-CLI, performance, and AI-assisted operations.

whatIDo.title: Lead the team. Own the customer experience.
whatIDo.description: Manage distributed hosting support engineers, own critical escalations, and keep customers informed. Hire, mentor, review quality, and turn recurring problems into better processes.

whatIDo.title: Find the problem beneath the symptom.
whatIDo.description: Trace production issues across Linux, Nginx, PHP-FPM, and MySQL/MariaDB. Bring logs, observability, root cause analysis, and cross-team coordination together during incidents.

whatIDo.title: Make WordPress more reliable.
whatIDo.description: Troubleshoot architecture, multisite, WooCommerce, plugin conflicts, and migrations. Tune caching, DNS, CDN, and database behavior around the actual workload.

whatIDo.title: Investigate. Clean up. Harden.
whatIDo.description: Investigate compromised WordPress sites, review suspicious files, and support recovery. Address infection vectors, firewall rules, brute-force mitigation, and vulnerability remediation.

whatIDo.title: Turn repeated work into useful tools.
whatIDo.description: Build Bash scripts, Ansible workflows, REST API integrations, and internal tools. Use AI-assisted engineering to support investigation, documentation, and operational decisions.

speaking.headline: From production systems to the stage.
speaking.summary: I speak at WordCamps and developer events on what I deal with every day: WordPress security, WP-CLI, performance, hosting infrastructure, and AI agents for real operations. Talks are practical, story-led, and built from production work, not slides about slides.

past.title: From Infection to Protection: Mastering WordPress Malware Cleanup

talks.title: Beyond Chatbots: Building AI Agents That Actually Do Things
talks.abstract: What turns an LLM into an agent? Tool calling, MCP, memory, planning, and agent loops, shown through real developer workflows: inspecting Linux, calling APIs, working with WordPress, and reading logs. Plus the lesson most demos skip: when a shell script or Ansible playbook is still the better answer.

talks.title: I Gave an AI Agent SSH Access: Here's What I Learned
talks.abstract: AI agents on a real Linux server: gathering context over SSH, investigating high CPU, debugging WordPress, spotting suspicious files. Then the hard part: permission boundaries, command restrictions, secrets, human approval, audit logs, and rollback.

talks.title: Security Isn't a Plugin: Lessons From Real WordPress Incidents
talks.abstract: Stories from real compromised sites: the reused password, the patch that came too late, the "free" premium plugin, the developer's laptop. No fear-mongering and no product pitch, just what actually stops the next incident.

talks.title: WP-CLI Unleashed
talks.abstract: Managing WordPress from the command line: bulk operations, search-replace, migrations, and scripting routine work. Delivered at WordCamp Asia 2023 and WordCamp Nepal 2022; available as a hands-on workshop.

formats: Meetup talks, in person or online

bio.short: Aditya Shah is a Hosting Support Manager and DevOps Engineer at WPMU DEV and has organized the WordPress Bhopal community since 2015. In 11 years of speaking at WordCamps, colleges, and developer events, he has reached 50,000+ people with talks on WordPress security, WP-CLI, performance, and AI agents for real operations.
bio.long: Aditya Shah leads hosting support at WPMU DEV, where he manages a distributed team and stays hands-on with Linux infrastructure, incident response, WordPress security investigations, and automation. He has worked with WordPress since 2014, founded and still runs the WordPress Bhopal community (100+ meetups and events since 2015), helped run the WP Build Tour that introduced 1,500+ students to WordPress, and is part of the WordCamp Asia 2026 organizing team. He has spoken at WordCamp Asia, WordCamp Nepal, WordCamp Pokhara, WordCamp Kochi, and WordCamp Mumbai, at Build with AI by Google & Hack2Skill, and at many college events on WordPress, Linux, DNS, and how websites work. In 11 years of speaking he has reached more than 50,000 people. He also contributes to WP-CLI. His talks turn production lessons into practical takeaways audiences can use the following Monday.
